TTGR44 – Belerno Loop

Start: Dalgety Bay Sailing Club · Finish: Dalgety Bay Sailing Club

Scenery and points of interest

The Balerno Loop (TTGR44) is a varied 43.2-mile circular adventure linking the shores of the Firth of Forth with Edinburgh's urban neighbourhoods and the greener surroundings of the Water of Leith. Starting at Dalgety Bay Sailing Club, the ride heads through Inverkeithing before crossing the iconic Forth Road Bridge, offering an impressive experience high above the Firth of Forth. Once on the southern side, the route continues towards Cramond Brig and Silverknowes before making its way through Edinburgh.

The middle section takes riders through Dalry Road, Gilmore Park and Kingsknowe before joining the Water of Leith corridor towards Balerno. This provides a welcome change of atmosphere, exchanging the bustle of the city for a more peaceful, leafy setting alongside the river. The Water of Leith path is a particularly memorable part of the journey, although it can become muddy following wet weather. Balerno offers an opportunity for a well-earned lunch break, with Carlyle's Bar & Kitchen and the BREAKOUT Café at Currie Rugby Club among the suggested options.

The return journey heads north-west through Ratho Station and Kirkliston, passing Burnshot Bridge before reaching the Forth Road Bridge for a second crossing. From here, the route retraces its way through Inverkeithing to Dalgety Bay Sailing Club. Combining a major bridge crossing, Edinburgh's neighbourhoods, riverside surroundings and a journey through the countryside west of the city, this is a rewarding day out for tandem crews who enjoy variety and a sense of adventure.

  • Forth Road Bridge: Cross the Firth of Forth twice, enjoying the distinctive experience of cycling high above the water.
  • Cramond Brig and Silverknowes: Explore the northern side of Edinburgh before heading towards the city.
  • Water of Leith: Follow a greener riverside corridor towards Balerno, offering a contrast to the urban sections.
  • Balerno: A welcoming destination for a lunch stop, with Carlyle's Bar & Kitchen and BREAKOUT Café suggested for refreshments.
  • Ratho Station and Kirkliston: Travel through the western outskirts of Edinburgh on the return towards the Forth.
  • Return to Fife: Enjoy a second crossing of the Forth Road Bridge before completing the loop at Dalgety Bay.

Terrain and cycling difficulty

The Balerno Loop is a moderately difficult 43.2-mile ride combining urban cycling, riverside paths and longer connecting sections between towns and villages. Its varied character makes for an interesting day on the tandem, with the Water of Leith providing a particularly enjoyable change of surroundings. Crews should be comfortable with a longer outing and prepared for changing conditions along the way.

  • Distance: 43.2 miles (approximately 69.5 km), starting and finishing at Dalgety Bay Sailing Club.
  • Climbing and effort: The route travels inland towards Balerno before returning towards the Forth. Expect some undulating terrain and changes in elevation, although the total ascent and steepest gradients have not been established.
  • Descents: There are downhill sections as the route changes elevation, particularly on the journey between the inland areas and the Forth. Pilots should maintain a comfortable, controlled speed and communicate before braking or changing pace.
  • Roads and paths: The ride combines roads through Edinburgh and surrounding settlements with the Water of Leith path. Pilots should be prepared for junctions, changes of direction and transitions between different riding environments.
  • Water of Leith conditions: The path can become muddy in damp weather. Tandems are generally able to manage these conditions, although a clean afterwards may be necessary. Solo support riders using narrow tyres or slicks are advised that this section may be unsuitable.
  • Tandem considerations: The longer distance, bridge crossings, urban navigation and riverside path require good communication between pilot and stoker. Allow time for a relaxed lunch stop and maintain a steady pace, particularly where paths are narrow, uneven or muddy.

With its combination of Forth crossings, city riding and riverside exploration, the Balerno Loop offers an enjoyable and varied challenge for tandem crews looking for a longer day in the saddle.
